problem:
The acceleration $a$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
a(t)=⟨6t-2,4⟩.
$$

Given that the particle is at the position $(0,0)$ and has velocity $⟨1,\,4⟩$ when $t=1,$ calculate the position vector of $P$ at time $t.$
worked_solution:
To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector. To find the velocity vector, we first need to integrate the acceleration vector. 

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨6t-2,4⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int (6t-2)\,\text{d}t,\,\int 4\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨3{t}^{2}-2t+{C}_{1},\,4t+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $v(1)=⟨1,4⟩.$ Substituting $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =⟨3(1)^{2}-2(1)+{C}_{1},\,4(1)+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨1,4⟩ & =⟨1+{C}_{1},4+{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=0$ and ${C}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the velocity vector is

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =⟨3{t}^{2}-2t,\,4t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the position vector by integrating the velocity vector.

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨3{t}^{2}-2t,\,4t⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int (3{t}^{2}-2t)\,\text{d}t,\,\int 4t\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨{t}^{3}-{t}^{2}+{C}_{3},\,2{t}^{2}+{C}_{4}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(1)=⟨0,0⟩.$ Substituting $t=1,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(1) & =⟨(1)^{3}-(1)^{2}+{C}_{3},\,2(1)^{2}+{C}_{4}⟩ \\ ⟨0,0⟩ & =⟨{C}_{3},2+{C}_{4}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{3}=0$ and ${C}_{4}=-2.$ Therefore, the position of $P$ at time $t$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨{t}^{3}-{t}^{2},\,2{t}^{2}-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
